summary.text: Take \(n=8=2^3\), for which \(\Omega(8)=3\) is odd and at least three. Since \(\mu(8)=\mu(4)=0\), Möbius inversion gives \(a(8)=8!(H_8-H_4)=25584>0\), contradicting the predicted negative sign.

full_proof.text:
Let
\[
H_n=\sum_{j=1}^n \frac1j
\]
be the \(n\)-th harmonic number. The sequence is characterized by
\[
\sum_{k\mid n}\frac{a(k)}{k!}=H_n.
\]
If we put \(b(k)=a(k)/k!\), this relation becomes
\[
H_n=\sum_{k\mid n}b(k).
\]
Möbius inversion on the divisibility poset therefore gives
\[
b(n)=\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(n/d)H_d,
\]
and hence
\[
a(n)=n!\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(n/d)H_d. \tag{1}
\]
Here \(\mu\) is the ordinary Möbius function: \(\mu(1)=1\), \(\mu(p)=-1\) for a prime \(p\), and \(\mu(m)=0\) whenever \(m\) is divisible by the square of a prime.

We disprove the conjecture by taking
\[
n=8=2^3.
\]
The positive divisors of \(8\) are \(1,2,4,8\). Thus formula (1) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
a(8)
&=8!\bigl(\mu(8)H_1+\mu(4)H_2+\mu(2)H_4+\mu(1)H_8\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(8\) and \(4\) are both divisible by \(2^2\),
\[
\mu(8)=\mu(4)=0.
\]
Also, \(2\) is prime, so \(\mu(2)=-1\), while \(\mu(1)=1\). Consequently,
\[
a(8)=8!\,(H_8-H_4).
\]
The difference of these harmonic numbers is
\[
H_8-H_4=\frac15+\frac16+\frac17+\frac18.
\]
Using the common denominator \(840\), this is
\[
\frac{168+140+120+105}{840}=\frac{533}{840}.
\]
Since \(8!=40320=48\cdot840\), it follows that
\[
a(8)=40320\cdot\frac{533}{840}=48\cdot533=25584.
\]
In particular,
\[
a(8)>0,
\]
so the assertion \(a(8)<0\) is false.

On the other hand, \(\Omega(n)\) counts prime factors with multiplicity. Since \(8=2^3\), its prime factorization contains three prime factors when multiplicity is counted, and therefore
\[
\Omega(8)=3.
\]
Thus \(\Omega(8)\) is odd and is at least \(3\). For \(n=8\), the right-hand side of the conjectured equivalence is therefore true, whereas its left-hand side, \(a(8)<0\), is false.

Hence the claimed equivalence does not hold for every positive integer \(n\), and the conjecture is false.
